transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (Tidewater CTO), Sofia Alvarez (Head of Infrastructure), Liam O'Connor (Security Lead)

Summary: quick discovery on Private/VPC deployment options, network connectivity, region/residency, and security integrations.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Mark: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:12] Sofia: Hi all, Sofia here. We're the infra team for Tidewater.
[00:16] Liam: Liam from security, short but yes.
[00:18] Priya: Great, we'll run through a few questions to understand your network topology and constraints, and then talk about how Redwood Private can fit. This call is discovery so feel free to jump in.

[00:35] Jordan: High level, are you evaluating hosted or private or both? What drove this call?
[00:42] Mark: We looked at hosted first, but due to compliance and data residency for EU shipments we need a private deployment in eu-west-1, and our security team wants KMS-backed encryption and no public egress if possible.
[00:55] Sofia: Also we need to integrate with our existing VPCs, prefer not to open wide internet access, and curious about peering vs private endpoints.

[01:12] Priya: Okay perfect. Can you tell us current cloud setup? VPCs, use of TGW, and whether you use PrivateLink today?
[01:20] Mark: We run on AWS across eu-west-1 and us-east-1, main production in eu-west-1. We have TGW connecting several accounts, VPCs for services, and some PrivateLink endpoints for partner services. No OpenVPN or direct connect yet.
[01:35] Sofia: Our CIDRs are fairly standard, we can share ranges after the call. We generally avoid VPC peering at scale, we prefer TGW.

[01:48] Liam: From security side, we need customer-managed KMS keys, mTLS for service-to-service, audit logs pushed to our S3/Athena pipeline, and RBAC via SSO (SAML). Also need to confirm network egress is in-region.

[02:10] Priya: Redwood Private supports customer KMS + HSM for key management, and we can accept SAML SSO for people access. For networking, we support multiple connection patterns: VPC peering, Transit Gateway attachment, and PrivateLink (AWS NLB + interface endpoints) depending on your preference.
[02:28] Jordan: For in-region traffic, we can pin instances to eu-west-1 and avoid cross-region egress. There are some nuances with model variant availability — we'll make sure supported models are available in the region or provide a compatible variant.

[02:48] Mark: That last part is key. Latency is critical for request/response for our customer-facing tracking chat. What's the typical latency delta between hosted vs Private in-region?
[02:58] Priya: In our benchmarks, dedicated on-prem or Private in-region runs similar to hosted when adjacent — token latency is mostly runtime bound. Additional network hops add small overhead; with TGW or PrivateLink you should see single-digit ms for control plane and tens of ms for large generation, depends on size of model and sequence length.

[03:20] Sofia: We also use autoscaling across fleets, can Redwood Dedicated autoscale? Or if we go Private, do we manage the nodes?
[03:28] Jordan: Two options: Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity managed by Redwood with predictable throughput. Private can be our managed private control plane with customer-managed compute in your VPC (or Redwood-managed nodes that sit inside your VPC). For fully air-gapped or on-prem you run it yourself. We can propose a hybrid.

[03:48] Liam: For compliance, do you provide audit logs and how long do they retain? We need to push to our S3 for 12 months retention and meet SOC2 audit trails.
[03:58] Priya: Yes, Private offers configurable audit log forwarding. We can push to your S3 or a syslog endpoint; retention is up to you. We will share a SOC2 pack and the audit forwarding config.

[04:16] Mark: Network specifics — we'd prefer not to peer every account, TGW is likely. Does Redwood support TGW attachments?
[04:24] Priya: Yes, we support TGW. Typically we create a VPC in your account and attach it to TGW, or we can provide interface endpoints using PrivateLink. Each has tradeoffs: PrivateLink keeps traffic in a single account boundary and is simpler for cross-account access, TGW is better at scale but you manage routing.

[04:45] Jordan: Also note that NLB-backed PrivateLink will allocate ENIs in subnets; you'll need to open the endpoint security groups. For TGW, we rely on route propagation. Priya can sketch out both patterns.

[05:05] Sofia: That's helpful. I heard about port requirements and health checks — anything we should pre-open in our firewall?
[05:12] Priya: For PrivateLink, you typically allow TCP ports 443 outbound to the endpoint and the NLB health check port. For TGW-based model, we need certain ports for gRPC/HTTP, we'll include a checklist — I'll send a matrix.

[05:28] Liam: We also have a policy that secrets must be in our KMS and no private keys leave environment. How does Redwood integrate with customer KMS?
[05:36] Priya: We can use customer-managed KMS for data-at-rest and optionally for some signing flows. For HSM-backed keys, we have an integration pattern that uses delegated key wrapping — we'll share docs. There are a few ops steps to set up IAM roles and key policies.

[05:56] Mark: Are we able to pin models version-wise? We need reproducible outputs.

[06:00] Jordan: Yes, you can pin model versions and we support rollouts/canary. That's in the console for Dedicated and Private deployments.

[06:10] Mark: Great. On capacity, our peak is roughly 200 concurrent sessions with average generation lengths medium (about 256 tokens) and a few heavy batch jobs overnight. Any quick signal on required GPUs or instance types?

[06:22] Priya: We'll need sample qps and tokens per minute; as a rough estimate, for medium-size models we'd recommend a mix of A100 or H100-like instances for peak and cheaper T4/RTX for background tasks. We'll propose a sizing in follow-up.

[06:38] Sofia: Region constraints: EU shipments must remain in eu-west-1. Are there any limitations if we request all infra to be pinned to that region?

[06:45] Jordan: We can pin to eu-west-1; the main limitation is model availability for some bleeding-edge variants. We'll provide a list of verified models in eu-west-1 and fallback variants.

[06:58] Mark: If a model isn't available there, is cross-region fallback automatic or blocked by default? We prefer blocked for compliance.

[07:06] Priya: Default is configurable. You can configure strict residency so we won't fallback cross-region; if you permit it, we can do automated fallback to ensure availability.

[07:18] Liam: Encryption on the wire — do you support mTLS between our services and the Redwood endpoints?

[07:24] Priya: Yes, we support mTLS and can require client certs on PrivateLink endpoints. We'll document the cert rotation flows.

[07:36] Jordan: Let's talk cost tradeoffs briefly — Dedicated is predictable commit and lower per-token cost for heavy, steady workloads. Private with customer-managed compute gives you more control but you manage instance ops. Which way are you leaning?

[07:48] Mark: We like predictability but want to avoid ops overhead. If Redwood can manage the nodes inside our VPC with minimal ops involvement and meet our security requirements, that's appealing.

[08:02] Sofia: How does RBAC and SSO work for Private — can we integrate with our Okta?

[08:08] Priya: Absolutely, SAML SSO via Okta is supported, with SCIM for provisioning if you want. Role mapping can be done via SAML attributes.

[08:18] Liam: Any third-party attestations? SOC2, ISO?

[08:21] Jordan: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we have an ISO summary; we'll attach the pack.

[08:30] Mark: On network egress costs — if Redwood manages nodes in our VPC, do you still charge for egress?

[08:37] Jordan: Egress billing depends on hosting model. If nodes are in your VPC and you pay for the instances, egress is your cloud cost. For Redwood-managed Dedicated outside your account, egress flows are part of our service; we'll break down cost. We'll include a cost comparison table.

[08:56] Sofia: There's one more constraint: our internal policy forbids cross-account IAM roles that assume into a Redwood-managed account. We prefer all resources in our AWS account. Is that supported?

[09:07] Priya: Yes, we can run instances in your account and either run our agent to manage them or provide runbooks for self-managed. For full managed service in your account we do a read-only operator role approach; no cross-account assume is required if you prefer. We'll detail pattern options.

[09:26] Mark: Ok, sounds good. Let's talk about network setup steps and timeline. If we decide to pilot, what are the typical setup activities?

[09:34] Priya: Pilot typically includes: 1) exchange CIDRs and decide TGW vs PrivateLink, 2) provisioning VPC/subnets & security groups, 3) KMS key policy & IAM roles, 4) deploy a small test cluster and run sample benchmarks, 5) validation with security and performance, then ramp. Usually 2-4 weeks for pilot depending on approvals.

[09:58] Jordan: We'll prepare a pilot plan and proposed timeline.

[10:02] Liam: For benchmarks, can we run an in-situ workload? We want to measure p95 latency for our chat flow.

[10:08] Priya: Yes, we can run benchmark harness against the deployed instance inside your VPC and produce p50/p95/p99 numbers and token cost estimates.

[10:18] Mark: From procurement perspective, who will sign? We'll likely need a PO and security questionnaire.

[10:23] Jordan: We'll send standard procurement docs and our security packet. We'll also include contract templates for Dedicated/Private.

[10:31] Sofia: A few small questions: do you support VPC endpoint policies for restricting access to endpoints per-role?

[10:36] Priya: Yes, you can set endpoint policies and SG rules to limit access.

[10:40] Mark: If we choose PrivateLink, how do updates/patching occur? Will there be maintenance windows?

[10:46] Priya: For customer-managed compute, you control maintenance windows. If Redwood manages nodes inside your VPC, we coordinate maintenance windows with you; for Dedicated we offer SLA with scheduled maintenance notifications.

[10:59] Jordan: Quick check — any blockers preventing a pilot?

[11:02] Mark: Need internal approvals but network & security look plausible; we'll need the checklist and pricing to push it forward.

[11:09] Sofia: Also need to confirm model availability in eu-west-1.

[11:12] Priya: We'll include verified model list for eu-west-1.

[11:16] Liam: And SOC2 docs + KMS integration guide.

[11:19] Jordan: Got it. We'll follow up with the items.

[11:22] -- brief technical digression --
[11:30] Priya: For the technical folks — high level architecture: we can deploy a control plane that talks to your model workers over ENIs inside your VPC. Model workers can be autoscaled; KV cache and prefix caching can be local to reduce repeated loads. We'll send an architecture diagram.

[11:52] Mark: On caching — if we do prefix caching, will that store any PII? We need to ensure PII minimization.

[11:59] Priya: Caching can be configured to ignore or redact PII. We also support ephemeral KV caches that are not persisted. We'll include config options.

[12:12] Sofia: Any constraints with our existing firewall appliance?

[12:16] Priya: As long as the necessary ports and endpoint SGs are open, it should be fine. We'll provide a port checklist.

[12:25] Jordan: Okay, let's recap next steps.

[12:28] Jordan: Action items - Jordan to send checklist and pricing; Priya to prepare sizing and model availability in eu-west-1; Mark to share CIDRs and authorization for pilot account.

[12:40] Mark: Sounds good. One more question around latency budgets — what's a realistic p95 for a 256-token generation on a medium model?

[12:47] Priya: For a 13B-ish open model on A100 in-region you could expect p95 ~200-300ms for short responses, longer for 256 tokens — depends on batching. We'll capture concrete numbers in the benchmark.

[13:05] Liam: Ok we need to review the benchmark results with security.

[13:08] Jordan: Understood. We'll coordinate. Thanks everyone, we'll send the follow-up email with docs and proposed times for the deep-dive.

[13:18] Mark: Thanks.

[13:20] Sofia: Thanks all.

[13:21] Liam: Cheers.

[41:30] END OF RECORDING

Notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings; speaker turns may be slightly off. References to TGW, PrivateLink, NLB, ENI, KMS, SOC2, SAML, SCIM, mTLS, KV cache. Links shared: Private deployment checklist (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/private-checklist), SOC2 pack (link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2), model availability list (link: https://redwood.ai/models/eu-west-1).
